title: SUBSTITUTE vs REPLACE: by text or by position
meta_desc: SUBSTITUTE vs REPLACE in spreadsheets: one swaps known text, the other overwrites by character position. When to use each, verified across all three apps.
intro: They sound like synonyms; they're opposites in how they aim. SUBSTITUTE finds TEXT you know ("replace every dash") — REPLACE overwrites a POSITION you know ("replace characters 4-6, whatever they are"). Picking the wrong one is why the other one's arguments never seem to make sense.

cols: The old text and its replacement
Start position, length, and the new text
All by default; the 4th argument picks the nth
Strip symbols, swap separators, clean imports
Mask digits, fix fixed-width codes, insert into IDs
Universal (every version of all three apps we test)

when.use_when: You know WHAT to change: remove commas, change "/" to "-", swap CHAR(10) line breaks. If the text moves around, SUBSTITUTE finds it anyway.
You know WHERE to change: overwrite characters 5-8 of a fixed-format code, mask a card number (=REPLACE(A2,1,12,"************")), or insert text at a position (length 0).

compat_note: Both execute identically in every version of Excel, Google Sheets, and LibreOffice we test. One cross-app note: Google Sheets' REGEXREPLACE covers both jobs (and more) but is Sheets-only — formulas using it break on export.
